author: Sofia Alvarez Entertainment Editor
title: BABYMONSTER's Asa Sparks Fan Comparisons to Resident Evil's Ada Wong
text:
K-pop star Asa of BABYMONSTER has become an unexpected focal point of online discussion after fans noticed striking similarities between her appearance and Ada Wong, the legendary double-agent from the Resident Evil series. The comparisons, fueled by recent selfies posted on the group’s Weverse community, have ignited a wave of fan reactions, with some jokingly suggesting she could portray the character in a live-action film.
Fan Reactions and Online Comparisons Asa’s distinctive look—characterized by a short bob, side bangs, and a penchant for deep red outfits—has long drawn comparisons to Ada Wong, a character renowned for her enigmatic style and espionage prowess. The latest round of fan speculation began after Asa shared selfies on the BABYMONSTER Weverse community, prompting comments like “Asa Wong ,” a portmanteau of her name and the character’s. One fan quipped, Asa, you are so much like Ada Wong, it’s insane. If you have a PS4 or PS5, go play Resident Evil 4 Remake! while another asked, Are you Ada Wong?
The resemblance isn’t new. Back in March, photos of the rapper surfaced showing her with a short bob and a black choker necklace, prompting fans to create endless side-by-side graphics with screenshots of Ada wearing her dress in Resident Evil 2 Remake . These visual parallels have cemented the connection in the minds of fans, with many expressing excitement over the potential for a crossover or cosplay.
Resident Evil Movie Context The buzz around Asa’s resemblance coincides with anticipation for the upcoming Resident Evil movie, directed by Zach Cregger. Scheduled to come to theaters this September, the film is set to diverge from the games’ established lore, with Cregger emphasizing that it will not feature direct adaptations of the series’ iconic characters. I am not trying to adapt a video game. I'm not using the characters from the games, Cregger stated at San Diego Comic-Con 2026. The games are so well executed, and to me, Leon and Claire and these characters, they exist so perfectly in the games that anyone I cast and any difference that I do with them would be, probably, to the detriment of what I was trying to do.

Despite the film’s departure from the games, fans have not abandoned hope of seeing Ada Wong in some form. However, Asa’s lack of public comments on the comparisons has left the possibility of a live-action portrayal open to speculation. Unfortunately for Ada stans, it doesn’t look like she’ll be making an appearance, one article noted, referencing the director’s clear stance on the film’s narrative direction.
Asa’s Response and Future Implications Asa has not publicly addressed the comparisons, leaving fans to speculate about her stance on the growing online discourse. While some have encouraged her to embrace the likeness through cosplay, others have begged her to portray Ada Wong in a live-action film. The group, managed by HYBE (the parent company of BTS’ record label), continues to navigate the intersection of K-pop and global pop culture, with Asa’s high-profile appearance further blurring the lines between entertainment industries.
The situation highlights the enduring influence of Resident Evil ’s characters, particularly Ada Wong, whose design and personality have become cultural touchstones. For K-pop fans, the connection underscores the genre’s growing ability to intersect with video game and film franchises, creating new avenues for fan engagement and creative expression.
As the Resident Evil movie approaches, the conversation around Asa’s resemblance to Ada Wong is likely to persist, particularly if the film’s narrative decisions spark further fan theories. For now, the focus remains on the upcoming release and how it might reshape the franchise’s legacy. Meanwhile, Asa’s position within BABYMONSTER and her individual career will continue to be shaped by the unique blend of music, fashion, and pop culture that defines K-pop’s global appeal.
